_note: innoferra 10-01: plain-language metadata for every real-traffic replay in runs_v3.json (numbers come from runs_v3.json, produced on node 0008 by serving/minimax-m3.1/extract_runs.py). at = PDT time the run finished. protocol v3 = before Oct 1 04:30 PDT (replayed the requests production rejected with 429 + media-tag bug); v3.1 = current.

runs.name: Starting setup (old routing: sessions pinned by arrival)
runs.why: Traffic piled onto 2 of the 4 engines while the other 2 sat idle.

runs.name: Production-style numerics (FP8 KV cache, training-compatible mode off)
runs.why: FP8 cache holds half as many tokens, so cache hits fell to 83.5% and prompts had to be reprocessed. Quality was fine (GSM8K 96.7%).

runs.name: Dynamo KV-aware router (production's router), default affinity
runs.why: Load spread evenly but cache reuse collapsed to 65% (ours 94%): each engine has two separate caches and Dynamo did not pin the right one.

runs.name: Dynamo KV-aware router, strong affinity
runs.why: Cache reuse only recovered to 71%.

runs.name: Load-aware routing (new sessions to the least-busy engine, move overloaded sessions)
runs.why: Routing balanced all 4 engines, which exposed the real limit: every engine queued requests and decode fell to 38 tok/s.

runs.name: Load-aware routing
runs.why: Routing fixed the pile-up (2/15 → 7/15). Misses came from huge cold prompts and from 6 errors caused by a media-tag bug (fixed later).

runs.name: Load-aware routing
runs.why: Median TTFT just above 1 s and decode 53 tok/s: prompt processing pauses token generation on both GPUs of an engine.

runs.name: + more GPU memory for the cache (0.68 → 0.76)
runs.why: Fewer evicted sessions: median TTFT 1.19 → 1.01 s, 42% fewer first tokens over 10 s. Decode still below 60.

runs.name: + fair-share prefill (waiting requests get half of each prefill step)
runs.why: An engine ran out of cache memory mid-prefill and crashed. Root cause patched; the test is queued again.

runs.name: Load-aware routing (re-run on the current test)
runs.why: Same settings as 03:56 on the corrected test: 7/15 → 9/15. The 6 misses are slow-tail TTFT from 300k+-token prompts and one median miss.

runs.name: + shorter speculative-decoding blocks (DSpark block 7 → 4)
runs.why: The draft model's acceptance fell 3.66 → 3.06 tokens per step, so decode dropped 55 → 46 tok/s.

runs.name: + smaller prompt-processing chunks (32k → 16k)
runs.why: Slightly worse on TTFT and decode: smaller chunks add steps without cutting total prefill time.

runs.name: Adopted settings (load-aware routing + 0.76 cache memory)
runs.why: 13/15: both misses are median TTFT 1.02 and 1.05 s. Slow tail and decode beat production on the same requests.

runs.name: Adopted settings (load-aware routing + 0.76 cache memory)
runs.why: 10/15 (9/15 with the old memory setting): slow-tail TTFT improved 14.3 → 11.7 s; misses are 3 median-TTFT minutes just over 1 s and 3 slow-tail minutes.

runs.name: + longest-cached-prompt-first scheduling (on top of 0.76 cache memory)
runs.why: Same 1/15, but every rule improved: slow-tail TTFT 18.3 → 13.4 s, decode 55 → 57 tok/s, fewer failing minutes on each rule. Decode below 60 is still the main miss at this load.

runs.name: + 128 running requests per engine (64 per GPU)
runs.why: Both GPUs' schedulers died while capturing the CUDA graphs for 64 running requests each; the engines crash-looped and the run never started.

runs.name: + fair-share prefill, retried with the out-of-memory fix (on top of capacity + longest-prefix-first)
runs.why: No crash this time (fix works), but worse: slow-tail TTFT 13.4 → 18.5 s, median 0.98 → 1.03 s, decode 57 → 55 tok/s.

runs.name: Adopted settings + longest-cached-prompt-first scheduling
runs.why: 13/15 again: the two misses moved (median first token 1.19 s in minute 1, 1.02 s in minute 10). Our per-minute medians swing 0.63–1.19 s around the 1 s line, so the first-token floor itself must come down.

runs.name: Adopted settings + longest-cached-prompt-first scheduling
runs.why: 9/15, but the slow tail is fixed (worst first token 9.5 s, 0 minutes over 15 s). All 6 misses are the median first token just over 1 s — the per-request tokenisation floor.

runs.name: + 8 tokenizer processes (adopted settings + cache-first)
runs.why: 10/15 vs 9/15 with 4 processes: median first token 0.94 → 0.90 s and median misses 6 → 3 minutes, but 2 slow-tail minutes came back. Within run-to-run noise.

runs.name: + 1 tokenizer process with a larger tokenisation cache
runs.why: 1/15: median first token 1.26 s (0.90–0.94 with 4–8 processes). One process also carries all HTTP and streaming work, which outweighs its cache hits.

runs.name: + 8 tokenizer processes (adopted settings + cache-first)
runs.why: 13/15 again: misses are minutes 0 and 1 (median first token 1.02 and 1.11 s). Across four 1.79 M runs the misses sit in the first two minutes and are 0.02–0.19 s over the limit.

runs.name: + parallel tokenising (16 pieces)
runs.why: Aborted after 8 of 15 minutes: slowest-1% first tokens 25–60 s per minute (6–15 s without) and decode 54–67 tok/s; the extra tokenizer threads most likely starve the GPU scheduler processes. Retesting with 4 pieces.

runs.name: + parallel tokenising (4 pieces)
runs.why: 5/15 vs 10/15 without it: slowest-1% first tokens 15–28 s in several minutes. Even 4 pieces hurt the engine, so parallel tokenising inside the tokenizer processes is dropped.

runs.name: + warm prompts step ahead of long uncached chunks
runs.why: 9/15 vs 10/15 without it: median first token over 1 s in 4 minutes (1.04–1.13 s), slowest-1% over 15 s in 2. Warm requests seldom wait behind uncached chunks, so the ~1 s median is not queueing.

runs.name: 8 tokenizer processes, repeat run (noise check)
runs.why: 11/15 on the settings that gave 10/15 earlier: identical runs differ by about one minute. Misses: median 1.10 and 1.05 s (minutes 0, 11); slowest-1% 16–24 s in minutes 11, 12, 14.

runs.name: + shared tokenisation cache across 8 processes
runs.why: 12/15 (same settings without it: 10 and 11). Every minute passes the median rule (worst 0.98 s); the 3 misses are slowest-1% only (21–24 s, huge uncached prompts). Kept as part of the tokenisation fix.

runs.name: + shared cache, no second tokenising pass
runs.why: 12/15 with median first token 0.54 s (0.85 with the shared cache alone; every minute 0.49–0.61 s) and overall p99 10.8 s (production 10.4). All 3 misses are the slowest-1% rule (16–22 s, huge uncached prompts).

runs.name: + one decode step after each prefill
runs.why: 15/15 under both the old strict rule and the new SLA; slowest 1% 8.2 s (production 10.4, without it 10.8) and every minute ≤ 14.5 s. Generation speed unchanged (76 vs 78 tok/s).

runs.name: production attention path, our 4-bit KV
runs.why: The engine refuses it: its fast 4-bit-KV path needs MiniMax's MSA kernel and does not allow speculative decoding. Stopped after 5 minutes; the 8-bit KV variant runs next.

runs.name: production numerics (attention + 8-bit KV)
runs.why: About 0/15 at 3.34 M: median first token 1.1–8.6 s and generation 45–66 tok/s per minute; 8-bit KV holds half the tokens, so prompts are re-processed (hit 91.2%). Replay tail cut 24 min after the window.

runs.why: 11/15 at 3.34 M (baseline 2/15): generation 64.1 tok/s per stream, production 64.8 on the same requests (+24%); acceptance unchanged 3.64, 0 errors. Minutes 9–12 still 50–55 tok/s.

runs.name: + pair the two GPUs' prompt pieces

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 7/15, generation 59.6 tok/s, median first token 1.53 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 12.3 M tokens.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 57.5 tok/s, median first token 1.57 s, 0 errors; uncached prompt 13.2 M tokens.

runs.name: + prompt chunks sized by cost
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation +2.69 tok/s (95% CI +1.6..+3.8), median first token −8% (CI −11..−4%), first-token p99 13.1 s vs 18.1 s; 7/15 vs 6/15. A prompt chunk over a long prefix costs far more (the indexer reads the whole prefix), so the chunk shrinks as the prefix grows: 16k tokens up to a 44k prefix, 5.9k at 200k. Both GPUs of an engine finish their step together more often.

runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU), cost-sized chunks with pivot 44k: 7/15, generation 55.8 tok/s, median first token 1.63 s, 0 errors (re-run after the 09:12 crash; the memory park fix was in place).

runs.name: + chunk pivot 88k instead of 44k
runs.why: Paired against the control on the same requests: generation +0.98 tok/s (95% CI +0.03..+1.98), first token −5.5% (CI −8.6..−1.5%); 6/15 vs 7/15. A pivot of 44k cuts chunks too hard; 88k keeps more of the gain. 88k is now the adopted value.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 55.7 tok/s, median first token 1.53 s, 0 errors.

Draft acceptance is the same (3.65). Each generation step costs more: the split needs an all-reduce in every layer. The next test adds production's fused all-reduce.

runs.name: control half at full load
runs.why: Control half at full load (4.42 M per GPU): 6/15, generation 58.2 tok/s, median first token 1.52 s, 0 errors.
